extracted.intended_audience: general readers seeking practical diet and physical-education guidance (late-19th-century popular audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical hygienic and dietary rules for preserving health and improving digestion as part of physical education: guidance on stimulants, meal timing/frequency, food selection, children's feeding, and corrective measures for overeating/dyspepsia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a firm stand against the poison-habit (avoid stimulants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every stimulant is, strictly speaking, a poison; avoid alcoholic and narcotic drinks, tobacco, and other stimulants because persistent use produces physiological dependence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains mechanism of addiction: initial adverse reactions, gradual adaptation of the organism, increasing doses required, eventual exhaustion of natural strength and difficulty of withdrawal. Examples: laudanum, arsenic, opium, alcohol. Advice: total interdiction of alcohol preferable; abstinence is easier than temperance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and avoid the progressive nature of stimulant use
rubrics_metrics.description: Mild stimulants and condiments pave the way to stronger substances; initial moderate use soon palls and leads to craving for stronger stimulants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: coffee, tea, and tobacco may lead toward opium in the East and alcohol in the West; pungent spices (pepper, mustard) are vanguard of the 'poison-fiend' by inflaming digestion and blunting taste. Avoid initiating habits that promote progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pungent condiments and hot spices
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from using pungent condiments and spices because they irritate the digestive organs and promote morbid appetites and gluttony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains physiological harms: inflame liver, produce stomach irritability, impede assimilation, blunt gustatory nerves, and lead to reliance on condiments rather than natural flavors. Anecdotes (e.g., peppered pickles blistering a Kiowa) illustrate unsuitability for many.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sparing in the use of animal food (especially in summer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit consumption of animal foods; consume them more sparingly in warm weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a general rule; rationale: animal food is heavier/harder to digest and summer favors lighter fare (eat fruit with every meal in midsummer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include unprepared foods (fresh milk, fruits) regularly
rubrics_metrics.description: Let unprepared food—fresh milk, fruits, etc.—form part of your daily fare; among unprepared and unspiced viands the most palatable are the most wholesome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates fresh, simple foods over heavily prepared or spiced dishes; gives example menus and suggests these foods aid digestion and health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer highly digestible, wholesome menus (ordered by digestibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose foods in the order of digestibility and wholesomeness: milk, bread, and fruit; eggs (raw or whipped), bread and honey; boiled eggs, bread and apples; bread and butter, rice pudding with milk; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full list of hygienic menus is provided, arranged from most to less digestible (includes fish, oatmeal-porridge, pancakes with honey, vegetable soups, baked beans, potatoes). Use these as templates for meals aimed at good digestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eat slowly and masticate thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Consume food slowly and chew it well to promote digestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among general rules; implicit anti-pattern: bolting food leads to indigestion and poor assimilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never eat if you have no appetite (respect natural appetite/aversions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not force yourself to eat when you lack appetite; respect intuitive dislikes and aversions which may indicate constitutional issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that lack of appetite can be a normal response to bodily needs (repairs, teething, effusions). Warns against forcing children or adults to eat foods they are repulsed by; gives examples where aversions correlate with severe physiological reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish your last meal at least three hours before bedtime
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow a gap of about three hours between your last meal and going to bed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of general rules; reason: ensures digestion is underway and avoids nocturnal indigestion/somnolence interfering with rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never stint the supply of fresh drinking-water (cold water is not dangerous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide ample fresh drinking water; the danger of water-drinking in warm weather has been exaggerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counters popular fears about cold water and cold air; advises abundant water intake in warm weather and rejects the idea that Nature punishes natural appetites for water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never eat until you have leisure to digest (allow post-meal rest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not eat when you will immediately be occupied with strenuous physical labor or intensive mental activity; digestion requires leisure and rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives experiment on dogs showing exercise after a meal prevents digestion; warns railroad laborers and brain-workers against eating during hard work or immediately before mental tasks. Recommends quiet rest after a hearty meal rather than immediate activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exercise immediately after a heavy meal; rest promotes digestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-meal exercise inhibits digestion; confinement/rest allows proper assimilation of food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Jules Virey's experiment: a dog that ran after a meal showed undigested food while a kennel-dog had completely digested the same meal. Advises against the myth that exercise after dinner promotes digestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lengthen the interval between meals; two meals a day may suffice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce meal frequency by lengthening intervals; two (or even one) meals may be adequate depending on training and habit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues principal meal should be the last of the day; gives historical and cross-cultural examples (Greeks, Romans, Claude Bernard) and suggests the human system is plastic and can adapt to fewer meals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fasting combined with outdoor exercise to correct surfeit/dyspepsia
rubrics_metrics.description: A fast-day spent in cheerful outdoor exercise is an effective peptic corrective for children and adults who have overeaten or suffer dyspepsia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports that a fast plus exercise diverts mind from food and aids digestion recovery; suggested as a nearly infallible remedy for children's temporary surfeit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an absolutely non-stimulating chiefly-vegetable diet plus open-air exercise to cure dyspepsia
rubrics_metrics.description: For chronic dyspeptics, an entirely non-stimulating mostly-vegetable diet together with active outdoor exercise can cure the condition within a single season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommends such regimes for boarding schools to become dietetic sanitariums; contrasts with stimulant-laden diets that perpetuate digestive disorders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not cram or force-feed children; avoid involuntary feeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid forcing children to eat against natural antipathies or beyond the point of repletion; involuntary cramming leads to morbid habit of overeating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that forced feeding can suspend natural satiety signals and cause a child to adapt to abnormal eating levels; suggests enticing children to play if they dally or refuse food rather than compelling them to eat.

rubrics_metrics.name: School-children: outdoor recess and light midday snacks (biscuit/apples) rather than heavy lunches
rubrics_metrics.description: Children should spend recess in outdoor play; a biscuit and apples will satisfy temporary hunger and prevent post-meal somnolence that dulls afternoon lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates avoiding heavy noon meals for schoolchildren; suggests pocketful of apples and light snacks; warns against pocket-flasks and cocktails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aphoristic planning: 'An hour of exercise to every pound of food'
rubrics_metrics.description: Match physical activity to food intake—a rough principle being an hour of exercise for every pound of food consumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented among dietetic aphorisms to emphasize exercise as a counterbalance to food intake; part of broader counsel linking activity and digestion.
